newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares play catch-up to U.S. in early trade.
newsitem.headline: German shares play catch-up to U.S. in early trade.

text.p: German shares got an early lift on Tuesday from overnight Wall Street gains and a firmer dollar as traders debated whether the DAX index has found a bottom or more losses are ahead.
The 30-share DAX index rose 47.64 points to 3,327.54 points in early bourse trade after reaching an initial high at 3,337.01 points.
The IBIS DAX, which reflects all-day trade and rose in post-bourse trade on Monday along with Wall Street, was up 30.16 points at 3,327.68 points.

Dealings were expected to focus on the release at 1230 GMT of U.S. consumer price data and its impact on market sentiment as to whether the Federal Reserve would have more scope to raise short-term interest rates at its next meeting in May.

But some traders said the German market was still underpinned by domestic fundamentals, including the weaker mark and relatively low interest rates, and that the DAX should remain between 3,200 and 3,400 points in the near-term.
Carmaker shares were at the forefront, with Volkswagen AG, BMW AG and Daimler AG all posting gains based on support from the dollar trading at about 1.73 marks in Europe.

The gains came despite the European car manufacturers' association ACEA saying on Tuesday that west European car registrations fell three percent year-on-year in March to 1.24 million units, with market leader VW posting no growth.
Among other top performers, engineering group Linde AG rose 40 marks to 1,146 marks, while software group SAP rose 8.20 marks to 283.50 marks.

Adidas was up 3.70 marks at 185.50 marks after the sportswear group said it would seek shareholder approval for a capital rights issue. Rival Puma AG also rose as the two groups outpaced the overall market gain.
